pois.name: Poseidon carbonate tower
pois.note: The published field position is a rounded 30°07'0"N 42°07'0"W (= 30.1167, -42.1167), which is also the data/landmarks.json pin; on this tile that point reads 1,332 m, on the massif's south wall, far outside the field's real 750-900 m depth range. The nearest terrain in the correct depth band is about 665 m north of that pin. This POI is placed there instead; seabed here is 801 m, and depth_m (775 m) sits partway up the ~60 m tower. See sources.md.

pois.name: Beehive chimney
pois.note: Beehive was a roughly 1 m vent on Poseidon; Aquino et al. 2024 report the chimney was absent by the 2018 visit. This separately scannable marker is placed illustratively about 140 m from Poseidon, not at a surveyed Beehive footprint.

pois.name: IMAX Tower
pois.note: IMAX is a parasitic chimney and flange on Poseidon's north face; a 2005 account gives about 8 m and a 2016 survey describes a roughly 30 m multipronged structure. This separate marker is placed illustratively near Poseidon.

pois.name: Microbial biofilm sampling site
pois.note: Coordinate near an OBIS occurrence cluster (2003 International Census of Marine Microbes samples) inside this bbox; nearly all records are archaea/bacteria with no reported depth. The visible mat/biofilm is an invented reconstruction; the sampling location is real.

pois.name: Atlantis Massif summit
pois.note: Real GMRT terrain: the shallowest point in this tile, 724 m, on the domed summit of the Atlantis Massif oceanic core complex. This is survey data, not a reconstruction.

pois.name: South wall (catalog position)
pois.note: The rounded 30°07'N 42°07'W field coordinate used by Wikipedia and data/landmarks.json lands here: real GMRT terrain on the massif's steep south wall, 1,332 m deep, about 665 m south of the actual vent field. Kept as a POI to show players the discrepancy directly. This is survey data, not a reconstruction.
